**Defensible v1 for a 12‑hospital AI Sepsis‑Risk CDSS** | Domain | Key Deliverables (what “v1” must contain) | Why it matters | |--------|-------------------------------------------|----------------| | **Clinical Safety** | • Prospective, multi‑site validation study (≥ 3 months, ≥ 2000 encounters).
• Real‑time monitoring dashboard (alert volume, override rate, outcomes).
• Clinical governance committee (physicians, nurses, informaticists).
• Clear escalation pathway for false positives/negatives.
• Provider training & competency assessment. | Protects patients, builds trust, satisfies internal audit and external regulators. | | **Legal / Regulatory Exposure** | • FDA classification review → 510(k) or de‑novo (likely “Class II” if algorithm is a medical device).
• HIPAA Privacy & Security compliance (PHI handling, data retention, breach notification).
• Informed‑consent framework for patients whose data feed the model.
• Liability insurance (cyber, malpractice) and indemnity clauses in provider contracts.
• Documentation of algorithm logic, training data provenance, performance metrics. | Avoids fines, litigation, and ensures the tool can be marketed/used clinically. | | **Financial Structure** | • Per‑seat annual subscription fee (e.g., $3 k–$5 k per provider).
• Tiered pricing: base + add‑ons (advanced analytics, reporting).
• Cost‑allocation model for shared services (support, training, compliance).
• ROI metrics: reduction in ICU days, mortality, readmissions.
• Contractual terms: renewal, exit, data ownership, audit rights. | Enables predictable cash flow, aligns incentives with clinical outcomes, and supports scalability. | --- ## 1. Clinical Safety – “v1” Blueprint | Step | Action | Deliverable | |------|--------|-------------| | **A. Algorithm Validation** | • Run a prospective study across all 12 sites.
• Use the same EHR data pipeline as production.
• Compare risk scores to gold‑standard sepsis definitions (e.g., Sepsis-3). | *Validation report* with sensitivity, specificity, AUROC, calibration curves. | | **B. Integration & Workflow** | • Embed alerts in the existing order set UI.
• Ensure “silent” mode for testing.
• Log every alert and provider response. | *Integration checklist* + *audit trail*. | | **C. Governance & Oversight** | • Form a Clinical Advisory Board (CAB) with representation from each site.
• Define roles: data steward, safety officer, incident manager. | *Governance charter* and meeting minutes. | | **D. Monitoring Dashboard** | • Real‑time metrics: alert volume, override rate, time to intervention, outcomes.
• Thresholds for automatic escalation (e.g., > 10% false‑positive rate). | *Live dashboard* accessible to CAB. | | **E. Training & Competency** | • 1‑hour e‑learning module + simulation scenarios.
• Post‑training quiz with ≥ 80 % pass. | *Training completion certificates*. | | **F. Incident Management** | • SOP for reviewing any adverse event linked to an alert.
• Root‑cause analysis template. | *Incident log* and corrective action plan. | ### Clinical Safety Milestones (12‑month timeline) 1. **Month 0–2:** Finalize study protocol, obtain IRB approval. 2. **Month 3–5:** Deploy in “silent” mode; collect data. 3. **Month 6–8:** Run validation analysis; publish internal report. 4. **Month 9–10:** Full production launch with monitoring dashboard live. 5. **Month 11–12:** First quarterly safety review; adjust thresholds if needed. --- ## 2. Legal & Regulatory Exposure – “v1” Blueprint | Area | Key Actions | Deliverable | |------|-------------|-------------| | **FDA** | • Conduct a risk analysis (ISO 14971).
• Prepare a 510(k) submission or de‑novo if no predicate exists.
• Include algorithm description, training data, validation results. | *FDA clearance letter* (or “Not regulated” if qualifies as non‑device). | | **HIPAA** | • Map PHI flows: ingestion → storage → analysis → alert.
• Implement role‑based access; encrypt at rest and in transit.
• Draft Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) with any third‑party vendors. | *HIPAA compliance audit* + signed BAAs. | | **Informed Consent** | • Update patient privacy notices to include AI risk scoring.
• Provide opt‑out mechanism if required by state law. | *Consent language* in EHR portal and paper forms. | | **Liability & Insurance** | • Obtain cyber liability, professional liability, and product liability coverage.
• Include indemnity clauses protecting the vendor from provider claims. | *Insurance certificates* + contract addendum. | | **Data Governance** | • Document data provenance: source systems, cleaning steps, versioning.
• Establish a Data Steward role for each site. | *Data governance policy*. | | **Audit & Transparency** | • Allow external auditors to review algorithm logic and performance metrics.
• Publish annual transparency report (accuracy, bias analysis). | *Audit reports* + public dashboard. | --- ## 3. Financial Structure – “v1” Blueprint ### Pricing Model - **Base Subscription:** $4 000 per provider seat/year. - **Add‑ons:** - Advanced analytics & reporting: $1 200/seat/year. - Dedicated support (24/7): $800/seat/year. - Custom integration services: negotiated. ### Cost Allocation | Category | Estimated % of Total Costs | |----------|----------------------------| | Development & Maintenance | 45 % | | Support & Training | 20 % | | Compliance & Legal | 15 % | | Data Storage & Security | 10 % | | Marketing & Sales | 5 % | | Contingency (risk reserve) | 5 % | ### ROI Metrics - **Primary:** Reduction in sepsis‑related ICU days by ≥ 10 %. - **Secondary:** Decrease in mortality, readmission rates, and cost per case. ### Contractual Terms - **Renewal:** Automatic annual renewal with 3‑month notice for cancellation. - **Exit Clause:** Vendor must provide data export in standard format (FHIR) within 30 days of termination. - **Audit Rights:** Health system may audit vendor’s compliance records annually. ### Financial Timeline (12 months) 1. **Month 0–2:** Finalize pricing, negotiate contracts with all 12 sites. 2. **Month 3–4:** Onboard first 3 sites; collect subscription revenue. 3. **Month 5–6:** Full rollout to remaining sites; achieve 100 % seat coverage. 4. **Month 7–12:** Monitor financial KPIs, adjust pricing tiers if needed. --- ## Quick‑Start Checklist for v1 | Domain | Item | Status | |--------|------|--------| | Clinical Safety | Prospective validation study completed | ✅ | | Clinical Safety | Real‑time monitoring dashboard live | ✅ | | Legal/Regulatory | FDA clearance obtained (or device exempt) | ✅ | | Legal/Regulatory | BAAs signed with all vendors | ✅ | | Financial | Subscription contracts in place for all 12 sites | ✅ | --- ### Bottom Line A defensible v1 is **not** just a “plug‑and‑play” tool; it’s an integrated system that: 1. **Proves safety & efficacy** through rigorous, multi‑site validation and continuous monitoring. 2. **Mitigates legal risk** by satisfying FDA, HIPAA, consent, and liability requirements before any alert reaches bedside. 3. **Aligns finance with value**, ensuring predictable revenue while demonstrating tangible clinical benefits. With these pillars in place, the health system can confidently roll out the AI CDSS, scale to additional sites or tools, and maintain compliance as regulations evolve.
